newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank accepts BIS membership.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank accepts BIS membership.

text.p: Slovenia's central bank said on Wednesday it had accepted an invitation to join the Basle-based Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
In a statement the Bank of Slovenia said it would buy 10 BIS shares at a price of $12,294 each by May 30.
Last week BIS invited the central banks of Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia to join but left out the National Bank of Yugoslavia.
The former Yugoslavia held 8,000 BIS shares which were suspended in June 1992 after the violent break-up of the country in 1991.

BIS said it would cancel the four states' new shares and divide the suspended Yugoslav shares between them and the rump Yugoslavia once the former Yugoslav republics reached an agreement on the division of assets of the former federation.

Assets, held at BIS, are estimated at about $660 million, but the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia has not been willing to participate in negotiations on their division, claiming it was the sole successor of the former federation.
